stories.title: Big Earthquake Shakes Indonesia's Flores Island
stories.headline_kid: A powerful earthquake hit an island in Indonesia, and rescuers are still digging through rubble to find people who are trapped.
summary: On Saturday, a huge earthquake measuring 7.7 on the scale struck near Flores Island in Indonesia, one of our neighbouring countries. So far, at least 47 people have died, and rescuers are still searching through collapsed buildings and a damaged port for survivors.

Indonesia sits on something scientists call the 'Ring of Fire' — an area around the Pacific Ocean where earthquakes and volcanoes happen often, a bit like how certain parts of a trampoline shake more when you jump near the edge. A second strong quake was also felt far away on Sumatra island, but luckily no damage was reported there.
Rescue teams are using helicopters and even a plane to reach hard-to-get-to areas and bring help faster. This is important because every hour matters when people are trapped under fallen buildings.

Indonesia is right next door to Singapore, and many Singaporean families travel there for holidays, especially to places like Bali. When disasters happen nearby, Singapore often offers help, showing that being good neighbours means looking out for each other even across the sea.

lenses.me: If your family has visited Indonesia before, this shows why checking travel news matters before a trip.
lenses.family: Parents might feel extra cautious about booking holidays to earthquake-prone areas for a while.
lenses.friends: Classmates with relatives in Indonesia may feel worried and could use a kind word from you.
lenses.nation: Singapore has helped nearby countries during disasters before, showing our country's role as a caring neighbour.
lenses.world: This earthquake reminds everyone how unpredictable nature can be, especially in this part of Asia.

stories.title: Lions Fall Behind in Big Football Battle with Thailand
stories.headline_kid: Singapore's football team, the Lions, lost 3-1 to Thailand in the first half of a huge two-part match, but the fight isn't over yet.
summary: On Saturday night, Singapore's national football team played Thailand at Jalan Besar Stadium in the first leg of the ASEAN Championship semi-finals. Thailand won 3-1, with their striker Teerasak Poeiphimai scoring twice in the first half alone.

Things got tougher for Singapore when striker Shawal Anuar's penalty kick was saved by the Thai goalkeeper. Thailand's captain then scored a third goal after the break, sealing a strong lead heading into the second match.

In this kind of competition, two matches are played and the scores are added together — this is called an 'aggregate' score. That means Singapore still has a chance to turn things around if they can score enough goals in the second leg.

This extends Thailand's winning streak against Singapore to 11 matches, and Singapore hasn't beaten them in about 14 years. Still, coach Gavin Lee has reminded the team that this losing run does not define who they are — there's always a next match to fight for.

lenses.me: Even when you lose the first round of something, you can still work hard for a comeback.
lenses.family: This could be a great match to watch together on TV and cheer for the Lions as a family.
lenses.friends: You and your classmates might be talking about this match at school on Monday!
lenses.nation: Football matches like this bring Singaporeans together to support our national team.
lenses.world: The ASEAN Championship shows how countries in our region compete in friendly sporting rivalry.

stories.title: From One Singapore Building to 1,000 Homes Around the World
stories.headline_kid: A Singapore company called Ascott started with just one building in 1984 and now runs more than 1,000 properties across the globe.
summary: Ascott is a Singapore company that began in 1984 with a single serviced residence — a place a bit like a hotel, but designed for people staying longer, like a home away from home. Today, Ascott operates over 1,000 properties in cities all over the world.

Their CEO, Kevin Goh, explains that even though Ascott has grown huge internationally, Singapore is still where they test new ideas first before rolling them out elsewhere. It's a bit like practising a new recipe in your own kitchen before serving it to guests.

The way people use hotel rooms has also changed. In the past, a room was just for sleeping in after a day of sightseeing. Now, many travellers work remotely, stay longer, and want their rooms to feel more like real homes.
This is a proud example of a homegrown Singapore brand succeeding on the world stage, showing that a good idea started right here can grow into something used by people everywhere.

lenses.me: It shows that big ideas can start small — even from just one building in Singapore.
lenses.family: Your family might have stayed in a serviced apartment like Ascott's during a holiday without even knowing it started here!
lenses.friends: This is something to be proud of and share with friends — a Singapore brand known worldwide.
lenses.nation: Ascott's success shows how Singapore companies can compete and thrive globally.
lenses.world: It reflects a bigger trend of people blending work and travel in a more flexible way.

stories.title: South Korea Asks North Korea to Talk About Ending the War
stories.headline_kid: South Korea's president wants to sit down with North Korea and officially end a war that technically never fully stopped.
summary: The Korean War happened from 1950 to 1953, but it never officially ended — the two sides only agreed to stop fighting, called a ceasefire, without signing a full peace treaty. That means North and South Korea have technically still been 'at war' for over 70 years.

On Saturday, South Korea's President Lee Jae Myung proposed talks with North Korea to finally end the war for good. He said both sides should 'put down their intentions to threaten each other' and talk things through directly.
This comes at a time when North Korea has been growing closer to Russia, which worries many countries watching the region carefully. Peace talks like this could help calm tensions in East Asia.

Singapore has a special connection to Korean peace efforts — in 2018, our very own city hosted the historic meeting between US President Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, a moment that gave the world hope for peace. Today's news shows that hope for peace in the region is still alive.

lenses.me: Learning about this war helps you understand how conflicts can last a very long time before being resolved.
lenses.family: Your family might remember Singapore hosting the famous 2018 summit — a proud moment in our history.
lenses.friends: You and your classmates can discuss how important peace and dialogue are, even in disagreements at school.
lenses.nation: Singapore is proud to have played a small part in past peace efforts between these two countries.
lenses.world: If successful, formally ending the Korean War could reduce tension across all of East Asia.

stories.title: Malaysia's PM Promises a Bigger Fight Against Corruption
stories.headline_kid: Malaysia's Prime Minister says he'll crack down harder on corruption, even after his party lost several recent elections.
summary: Corruption is when people in power misuse money or their position for personal gain, instead of using it fairly for everyone. Malaysia's Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim spoke at his party's congress on Saturday, promising to fight corruption even harder in the coming months.

This comes after his party had three disappointing results in recent state elections. Despite this, Anwar said he would keep doing 'the right thing,' even if it costs him politically — meaning he's choosing to stick to his principles rather than just chase popularity.
He also mentioned that he has the backing of Malaysia's king, which adds extra support to his anti-corruption efforts.

Malaysia is Singapore's closest neighbour, connected by the Causeway that thousands of people cross every day for work and school. A stable and honest government in Malaysia matters to Singapore too, since our two countries trade, travel, and work together so closely.

lenses.me: This story shows why honesty matters, even when it's the harder choice.
lenses.family: Your family might discuss how leaders' decisions in Malaysia can affect things like the Causeway traffic or prices of goods.
lenses.friends: You can chat with friends about what fairness means, using this as a real-world example.
lenses.nation: Singapore benefits when our neighbours have strong, honest governments, since we work closely together.
lenses.world: This shows how leaders everywhere must sometimes choose between doing what's right and staying popular.
